Burkina Faso's transitional assembly has voted unanimously to ban all political parties, with interim president Ibrahim Traore arguing that politics divides rather than unites the country. 
Around 100 parties have been dissolved, including the 15 that were represented in parliament before the coup. 
The United Nations estimates that 40 to 60 per cent of Burkina Faso is now outside government control, with armed groups linked to al-Qaeda and ISIL holding power in areas where the state does not. 
Critics say the ban silences dissent whilst Russia-linked AI-generated videos flood social media, reshaping public perception.

Al Jazeera's Nicolas Haque reports.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Teachers in San Francisco have launched their first strike in nearly 50 years, shutting all 120 district schools and forcing roughly 50,000 students into remote learning. The United Educators of San Francisco is demanding fully funded healthcare and salary increases of 9 to 14 percent. The district, facing a $100m deficit and under state oversight, has offered a 6 percent pay rise and $24,000 healthcare benefit, but teachers rejected the proposal. Meeting the union's demands would cost an additional $92m.

Al Jazeera's John Hendren reports from San Francisco.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
As Britain's Labour government faces mounting pressure over the Epstein files scandal, the right-wing Reform UK party has declared itself on election "war footing". 
Leader Nigel Farage addressed supporters in Birmingham, where the party claims to now be Britain's largest by membership. 
Polling suggests Reform could win the most seats if an election were held today, though Farage acknowledges the party is only "halfway" ready to govern. 
The party has attracted defecting Conservative MPs and is positioning itself as an anti-establishment, anti-immigration alternative to Britain's traditional two-party system.

Al Jazeera's Rory Challands reports from Birmingham.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Ghislaine Maxwell, the associate and former girlfriend of the late Jeffrey Epstein, has refused to answer questions before a United States House of Representatives committee, but indicated that she may testify in exchange for clemency.
Maxwell, who was found guilty in 2021 for her role in helping Epstein sexually abuse teenage ⁠girls, invoked her Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination, lawmakers from the House Oversight Committee said on Monday.
“This is obviously very disappointing,” the committee’s chairman, Republican Representative James Comer, told reporters.
“We had many questions to ask about the crimes she and Epstein committed, as well as questions about potential co-conspirators,”
Maxwell, who is serving a 20-year sentence for sex trafficking at a federal camp in Texas, was subpoenaed to appear before the committee to discuss her relations with Epstein, but her lawyers said she would only testify if President Donald Trump granted her clemency.

title: Ghislaine Maxwell refuses to testify before US Congress, asks for clemency
